criteria.demonstration: Acquired and initialized sets are separate, with initialized subset acquired and dependency closure before every successful initialization. The actual staged owner publishes only after all four nodes are initialized. Native C17 callback-view clearing and reverse destruction are explicit discipline; an actual Rust local Drop comparison produces success and failed-initialization traces, but does not claim to encode an arbitrary C dependency graph or fallible destructor.

criteria.demonstration: The unchanged actual ow_construct/ow_destroy provider is composed with the actual typed ow_allocator through V4Allocator, with exact release ordering. The successor stores per-node initialized state, typed counts, acquisition order and callbacks. It validates all lengths/order/callbacks before effects, retains acquired raw storage during incomplete initialization, and preserves the public destination on either allocation or initializer failure.

criteria.criterion: Inject failure on each acquisition, reject zero and overflowing lengths before any callback, instrument release order and exactly-once counts, and test repeated destruction. Kill the omitted-rollback mutant. Extend the anchor with a callback trace that proves reverse order, not just equal release totals.

criteria.demonstration: Six C17 profiles execute five anchors, nine compiled semantic controls and five compiling-stub rejections. The independent902-history model covers all24permutations, all three valid topological orders, every allocation-failure position and initializer-failure node plus invalid/overflow/backend-too-large counts. Exact event streams, poison/live counts and repeated destruction distinguish reverse cleanup from equal totals. Actual OW_MUTANT1/11 are rejected separately; no sanitizer abort is accepted as mutant success.

criteria.criterion: Replace the prefix with a dependency graph: acquire A, then B and C independently, then D requiring B. Write an initialized-set representation and reverse dependency cleanup. Delayed assessment makes C initialization fail after its storage acquisition; distinguish storage release from destruction of a constructed value.

criteria.demonstration: The mandatory delayed graph A before B/C, B before D is implemented in all three valid orders. In A,B,D,C with C failing after acquired storage, releaseC occurs with no destroyC, followed by destroy/releaseD,B,A. Every destructor receives a view without itself but with still-live initialized dependencies. The independent seven-day learner variant remains unperformed; the author campaign supports only these bounded concrete graph/callback contracts.
